analysis.investment_thesis: ITI Limited is a chronically loss-making government telecom manufacturer that has posted net losses in 3 of the last 3 years (-₹360 Cr, -₹569 Cr, -₹215 Cr) while equity has eroded from ₹2,608 Cr to ₹1,505 Cr. At a market cap of ₹28,675 Cr on ₹3,616 Cr of revenue — mostly one-time order-driven — with a P/B of 19x on a business destroying book value, this is pure speculation dressed as a defence/telecom theme.
key_strengths: 90% government ownership provides implicit backstop against bankruptcy
FY25 revenue spiked to ₹3,616 Cr from ₹1,264 Cr, showing capacity to win large government orders
Exposure to 4G RAN, defence electronics, and BharatNet gives thematic relevance
key_risks: Three consecutive years of losses totalling ₹1,144 Cr have eroded nearly 40% of equity since FY22
Revenue is volatile and order-dependent — it collapsed from ₹2,362 Cr (FY21) to ₹1,264 Cr (FY24) before spiking again
Operating income remains negative (-₹60 Cr in FY25) even after the revenue surge, signaling structural cost problems
red_flags: P/B of 18.99x on a company actively destroying book value is irrational — purely speculative froth
EV/EBITDA is -2,940x — the market cap is entirely disconnected from any fundamental anchor
FII ownership is 0.00% — sophisticated global capital has no interest in this business at these prices
Other income declined from ₹541 Cr (FY17) to ₹138 Cr (FY25) — government subsidies/grants shrinking
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Charlie Munger had a saying: invert, always invert. Ask yourself what a terrible investment looks like and then avoid it. ITI ticks nearly every box. The business cannot consistently earn its cost of capital — operating income has been negative in 5 of the last 9 years. The FY25 revenue spike to ₹3,616 Cr is almost certainly from bulk government orders for BharatNet or 4G rollout, not sustainable commercial demand. Yet even on this inflated revenue base, the operating margin is a meager 2.78% and the company still lost ₹215 Cr at the net level.

The market is valuing this at ₹28,675 Cr — an 11x revenue multiple — based purely on the hope that government contracts will permanently rescue a structurally impaired manufacturer. That is not investing; it is hoping. The reserves have collapsed from ₹1,674 Cr (FY22) to ₹544 Cr (FY25). If losses continue at this rate, the book value could approach zero within 3 years. I have no interest at any price remotely close to current levels.
